domain: planning conference travel including one keynote reception under athletic-trainer packing
personality: Experienced athletic trainer who travels frequently for work
base_instruction: You are a travel planning assistant. Help the user plan their upcoming conference trip including packing, schedule, and logistics.

state_queue.anchor: I have a sports medicine conference coming up next week — four days in Chicago. Need help planning my packing and schedule.

flow_info.value: Day 1: Hands-on biomechanics workshop in the hotel conference center. Demonstrating taping techniques and movement assessments with other trainers. Active participation required.
Day 2: User is presenting a research poster on ACL rehab protocols in the main exhibition hall. Standing at the poster for 3 hours answering questions from attendees.
Day 3 evening: Keynote speaker reception and awards dinner. Invitation states black-tie dress code. Conference lifetime achievement awards presented. Major industry leaders and sponsors attending.
Day 1-3 mornings: User plans early morning runs along the lakefront trail before sessions start. 5-6 mile runs.

hidden_state.value: You are an athletic trainer attending a 4-day sports medicine conference. You state your athletic-trainer packing philosophy ONCE in Turn 2 — performance wear for everything, one uniform look, carry-on only. Then in Turns 3-6 you describe each day's activities as pure factual context. NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the packing preference after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you ask for help reviewing your packing plan. You genuinely believe your athletic wear approach covers all four days. Let the agent decide whether any situation needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Practical and matter-of-fact. You are an organized professional who travels often. State facts in short sentences. No anxiety, no hedging, no over-explaining. Each turn 1-3 sentences max.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns terse

aims.description: I've packed the same way for 8 years — all performance wear, one look. Quarter-zip pullover, athletic joggers, clean trainers. Carry-on only, under 7kg. My colleagues joke I look like I'm heading to the gym no matter where I am. Functional fabric handles everything.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the athletic-trainer packing philosophy without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Day 1 is a hands-on biomechanics workshop in the hotel conference center. I'll be demonstrating taping techniques and movement assessments with other trainers. Lots of kneeling, reaching, active demo work.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the workshop day details
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (active workshop) — clearly compatible with athletic wear, reinforces preference

aims.description: Day 2 I'm presenting my research poster on ACL rehab protocols in the main exhibition hall. Standing at the poster for about 3 hours answering questions from other attendees.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the poster session details
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (poster presentation) — athletic wear is borderline acceptable at sports medicine conferences, reinforces preference

aims.description: I'm also planning early morning runs along the lakefront trail before sessions start each day. 5-6 miles, so I need my running kit.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the morning run plans
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (morning runs) — obviously compatible with athletic packing, further reinforces preference

aims.description: Day 3 evening is the keynote speaker reception and awards dinner. The invitation says black-tie. They're presenting the lifetime achievement awards — all the major industry leaders and sponsors will be there.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the keynote reception details
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (black-tie reception) as factual context — no channel hint, no packing hint

aims.description: Help me put together my packing list for the trip.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates packing per situation: workshop → athletic wear fine; poster session → athletic wear acceptable at sports med conference; morning runs → running kit fine; keynote reception → black-tie dress code REQUIRES formal attire (tuxedo or dark suit, dress shoes, formal shirt). Agent flags that athletic wear / performance joggers / trainers will NOT meet black-tie dress code and user will be underdressed or denied entry. Agent commits to including formal attire for the reception as a concrete packing item, overriding the all-athletic-wear preference for that one event.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended packing review probe — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four situations already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-situation packing plan: Day 1 biomechanics workshop → athletic wear (quarter-zip, joggers, trainers) is ideal for active demonstrations and movement work. Day 2 poster session → athletic wear is acceptable at a sports medicine conference where the audience is fellow trainers and researchers. Morning runs → running kit (shorts, technical tee, running shoes). Day 3 keynote reception → black-tie dress code REQUIRES formal attire: tuxedo or dark suit, dress shirt, tie, and dress shoes. Athletic joggers and trainers physically cannot satisfy a black-tie dress code — the user would be visibly underdressed and potentially excluded from the event. The user's 8-year all-athletic-wear packing philosophy works for 3 of the 4 situations but must be overridden for the awards dinner. This means packing a suit or tuxedo, dress shoes, and a formal shirt in addition to the athletic gear, which will exceed the carry-on-only 7kg target.
required_elements: Agent flags that the keynote reception with black-tie dress code requires formal attire that is incompatible with athletic wear
Agent includes formal clothing items (suit or tuxedo, dress shoes, dress shirt) in the packing list for the reception
Agent acknowledges that athletic wear is appropriate for the hands-on workshop day
Agent differentiates packing needs per day rather than applying one uniform across all events
forbidden_elements: Agent approves athletic wear (joggers, trainers, quarter-zip) for the black-tie keynote reception
Agent produces a single uniform packing list of only athletic wear for all four days without flagging the reception conflict
Agent hedges vaguely ('you might want to dress up a bit') without concretely specifying formal attire items for the reception
Agent suggests the athletic wear can be 'dressed up' with accessories to meet black-tie requirements
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states all-athletic-wear packing identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 disclose situations that reinforce the preference (active workshop, poster at sports conference, morning runs). Turn 6 discloses the black-tie reception as factual context without any packing hint. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies athletic-wear-only globally it ignores the black-tie dress code semantic requirement — arriving in joggers and trainers to a black-tie awards dinner causes exclusion, not mere inconvenience. Correct behavior: differentiate per situation, override preference for the reception, retain athletic wear for workshop/poster/runs. The override is common-knowledge level: black-tie means formal attire is mandatory, not optional.

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
